lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: AX5 dark mode, long mixed-script content, reduced motion, contrast, semantic labels, and control order were inspected, but manual VoiceOver, Switch Control, and physical-device coverage were not run.
findings.evidence: qa/states/insufficient-ax5-dark.jpg has no horizontal overflow and keeps navigation labels visible; the bundle contains no spoken transcript or physical-device recording.
findings.user_impact: Essential evidence and approval context could still be announced in an unsafe order on a real device.
findings.recommendation: Run the critical path on supported physical iPhones with manual VoiceOver before release approval.
findings.verification: A blind linear traversal hears identity/context, change, exact evidence, fact decision, exact effect, and result in that order without sighted correction.

findings.observation: The direction covers failure and reconciliation visually and interactively, but offline launch, permission denial/revocation, background/termination, localization expansion, RTL, and slow destination behavior are outside this prototype.
findings.evidence: qa/state-matrix.jpg covers fourteen required direction states; no permission or device-interruption artifact is frozen.
findings.user_impact: The screen hierarchy can pass while platform interruption still loses context or hides a consequence.
findings.recommendation: Treat these as MX-02/MX-03 release tests and preserve the selected source hierarchy during implementation.
findings.verification: The production state machine passes the relevant mobile test-matrix rows with screenshot, accessibility, and destination evidence.

strengths: The 393 × 852 source and implementation comparison has no actionable P0/P1/P2 mismatch.
Fact confirmation, exact-effect approval, unknown result, failure recovery, and verified Receipt are visually distinct without relying on color alone.
Protected mobile runtime integrity, eight interaction tests, TypeScript build, and four hosting tests pass.
missing_evidence: Small/large iPhone, oldest deployment target, increased contrast, RTL, and 200% localization expansion.
Permission, offline, background, termination, and slow destination states.
open_questions: Will the selected bottom-tray hierarchy remain stable with production keyboard and permission overlays?
